label: Emergency Fund Before Debt
summary: The central perspective argues for building an emergency fund before aggressively paying down credit card debt to ensure financial stability and avoid incurring more debt from unexpected expenses. Establishing a modest emergency fund provides a financial cushion and peace of mind, protecting against financial disruptions. This approach is particularly advisable if you lack any savings or face variable income and near-term costs.
conditions: You have enough savings to cover necessary expenses.
If you don't have an emergency fund
caveats: Unexpected expenses can still arise, requiring careful planning.
Using savings to pay off debt can leave you without a financial cushion for emergencies.

label: High-Interest Debt First
summary: The central claim is that paying down high-interest credit card debt should be prioritized to save money in the long run. This approach is particularly beneficial when you have high-interest debt that costs more than potential savings earnings. It is suggested to focus on the highest interest or highest balance accounts first.
conditions: You have high-interest credit card debt.
You can make larger payments towards your debt.
caveats: Focusing solely on debt repayment may deplete your savings.
Be sure to keep paying all minimums on time.
